- scripts/security_audit.sh:1864-1874 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: Wrapper digests are rendered with the full SHA of the support checkout's HEAD (`managed-digests --commit HEAD`), so a consumer's unedited wrapper pinned to an older release SHA matches no digest. It is classified `modified` and filed as `consumer_modified`.
  WHY: The filter does not suppress the `*-runtime-support-ref-unpinned` wrapper findings for consumers on older releases, which is the case the PR targets. Severity disagreement: sonnet-5_5 rated NIT, minimax BLOCKER, luna and qwen MAJOR; the highest is used.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:1875-1877 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]

  WHY: When the builder fails, the filter silently turns off and operators cannot see the cause. All reviewers rated this NIT.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:1875-1879 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The `pattern_count` python one-liner runs with the caller's full environment, while the builder runs under `env -i`.
  WHY: The environment hygiene is inconsistent. It reads only a file the script itself wrote, so the impact is low. The anthropic reviewer raised it only as a hardening suggestion.
- tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py:3570-3576 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `inspect.signature(globals()[name]).parameters` is recomputed for every parametrize case in `main()`.
  WHY: It is a negligible CPU cost with no behavioural impact. Both reviewers rated it NIT; anthropic does not recommend a change.

  PROBLEM: Wrapper digests use the full SHA of the support checkout's HEAD, so a consumer pinned to an older release SHA matches no digest.
  WHY: The unedited wrapper is classified `modified` and logged as `consumer_modified`, and the `*-runtime-support-ref-unpinned` findings are filed. This fails open and the changelog documents it. A narrow fix would normalise the 40-hex pin before hashing.

It runs with the caller's full environment while the builder runs under `env -i`. Fix: prefix it with `env -i PATH="${PATH}" HOME="${HOME:-/tmp}"` (1 line). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
